## Implementation decides

Each implementation names in its description:

1. **the raft transport secret** beyond mTLS, if there is one, and its rotation on revocation; the raft wire between members and the frame of `admin.sock`
   (read-fence, admit, import) remain internal to the implementation: a format with a name and a version, no new HTTP routes. The copy transfer itself uses the explicitly declared GET /v1/copy of N2; the members of one
   store cluster are one implementation, a mix of languages — only by clients through `configstore:///`;
2. **the durability of the store** (fsync, raft snapshots: threshold, interval, tail) — a teaching store MAY be non-durable, and this is said in its description; there is no flag or environment variable that turns the barriers off (N1.3 `durability`);
3. **the connection accounting of the daemon** and overrides of the limits by deployment, `-tuning` for slow networks; the normative defaults are N1.3;
4. **how `backup` obtains a consistent state of a running daemon** (N2); the requirement on the copy is a norm of N2, not a choice.
5. **the format mark and the profile `file://`**: the values `format` and `version` of its mark `FORMAT` and which versions of its format the build reads (N1.3 `format`); the on-disk format of the profile `file://`; the command by which a copy of N1.3 `copy` is taken from a store `file://` (the form of the copy is a norm).
6. **mutual exclusion of runs** of `recover`, `restore`, `import` on one installation (a lock, a mark file) — the norm requires one attempt (N3 «Races: admittance and recovery transitions»), the way is a choice. This also declares exclusive live-daemon ownership of `-dir`, refusal of a second daemon and local operations, and release on every process termination by N1.3, and the form and place of the phase mark of `recover` (N3 «recover the store» step 1).
7. **the internal contract of `file://`** (item 5): the format of the profile `file://` is the implementation's own, not a public contract. Its description
   and the library API are written in the implementation's repository by the owner of this chapter before the code: the physical layer and the command layer — conditional
   `put`/`delete` with `guard`, the batch `batch`, CAS by version, `not_before`/`not_after`, outcomes and refusal words as at the store door (P/01.1 N1,
   N4; without retelling the norms), with vectors from its own code. Other processes of the implementation (the installer, the worker) read only
   the contract and the API; a mix of languages on `file://` is not supported — through `configstore:///`.
8. **the finite budgets of this chapter**: the response-write budget, the commit wait, the number of door attempts and the replay-processing limit (R035), the limit of `admin.sock` (R008), the disk and descriptor budgets (R036). Each MUST be finite and positive; this chapter sets no value, flag or default for them. The implementation declares the value; the threshold of production acceptance is approved separately from the implementation, and a claim of the candidate alone is not enough.

- **Order of service checks.** The request parsing of the service doors is chapter 1.1 N2.1 (query, the JSON of the body, the path byte for byte, HTTP, early refusal); deviations are below. | Phase | What is allowed | What is kept on a refusal |
|---|---|---|
| Isolation | Stop/cut off the old members, fix the immutable input and upper | The old data; the new group is not started yet |
| Check | Check all rows (form, key, size), the base, the epochs and upper, the uint64 bounds; families of rows — only `recover` of its own dump: for all rows — the row envelope, the key by the catalogue, the version, the size; schemas — only of the families of the store itself (P/01) and upper; the content of other families is not interpreted and is kept as is — schemas are the business of their owners; the copy `copy` knows no manifests (N1.3 `import`) | Neither the floor nor the rows are changed |
| New floor | Raise floor above upper durably, once; op: floor has its own replay id | On an unknown answer repeat with the same id, do not compute a new generation |
| Transfer | Keep the first new floor F1; write all other copy rows with their copy versions, excluding the old platform/epoch_floor; durable progress for continuation | A partial transfer is possible; ordinary writers are forbidden |
| Done | Check every non-floor input row and the saved new F1 row; allow the updated membership/writers | The former group stays cut off; only epochs not below floor are started — one issued with the old floor is lost (P/03.2 N3 «take_epoch(id)») |

**Membership outcomes.** After the request refusals of R016, an unfinished transfer gives R413. Otherwise a box joins its own id with 200 `{}` (R171), refuses a foreign id with 409 even with force (R308), refuses leave with 409 (R172) and admit with non-zero exit (R173). A door refuses join/leave with 409 (R087) and admit by R417. At a follower, own join/leave can reach the leader by R119; another member's join/leave on admin.sock and any admit refuse by R118/R235. A group peer may leave only itself; another id requires the leader's admin.sock (R214). At the leader, an id barred by leave gets 403 on join until admit (R058); a current id with the same Raft address joins with 200 and updates API (R178), another Raft address gets 409 (R179). A new member is accepted with 200 only within the declared size and with force for transitional evenness (R055/R056/R352). Leave of a known member gives 200 unless it is the last voter (R416); unknown id gives 409 (R310). Admit confirms permission to rejoin with exit 0, including a repeat for an already admitted correct id; it changes no rows and does not itself join the id (R177/R234). On an unknown join/leave/admit result the caller reads membership (R228/R234).

From Check until Done of import/restore/recover, a running daemon MUST keep the ordinary outcomes of status, rights and metrics; these diagnostic commands do not expose partially transferred rows. Availability and access failures of their own doors remain applicable.

A concurrent import, restore or recover on the same installation MUST refuse with non-zero exit without changing data. After interruption, the same input continues by R152, another input refuses by R153, and recover restarts by R339; concurrency is not continuation.

Leave of the last voter of a Raft group MUST return 409 `refused` without membership or row changes, including a one-voter group; force does not permit it. This is the same visible refusal as the box's R172.
Admit on a door without a vote MUST refuse with non-zero exit without changing membership or rows; it cannot grant admission through another instance.

During offline box import/restore or local recover, the daemon is stopped: status, rights, join, leave, admit, backup and all HTTP doors have no serving socket on that instance; no HTTP reply is promised. A start on an unfinished box transfer or a recover phase mark MUST refuse with exit 2 (R048/R267); startup after Done follows R292, subject to R341. A local command on a live-owned directory instead gives R185.

- `service_body_form`: service HTTP: unknown fields, not an object/not JSON, extra JSON, a detected framing violation or an inadmissible field. EOF/truncation follows R054 without an HTTP refusal; input-phase timeout is `input_timeout`. Caller action: fix the input; there is no side change.
- `service_body_limit`: service HTTP: a body larger than `-max-body`, whatever the method (R221). Caller action: shrink the body; the limit is by actual bytes.
- `floor_not_integer`: `op: floor`: `floor` is not a JSON integer (`2.0e1`, `20.0`). Caller action: an integer.

- `import_other_input`: `import`/`restore` with another input before «Done» of an unfinished attempt (N1.3 `import`); nothing changes. Caller action: repeat with the same input, or after `recover` a new full attempt.

- `copy_snapshot_unavailable`: a consistent copy cannot be obtained before successful headers within the declared wait, or the instance is a door (P/01.3-R411). Caller action: retry the read when available; no write outcome is ambiguous.
- `start_data_dir_owned`: a second daemon on a live-owned data directory (N1.3 «Data-directory ownership»). Caller action: do not take ownership; retry only after the owner exits.
- `local_data_dir_owned`: offline box import/restore or local recover on a live-owned directory (N1.3). Caller action: stop the owner first and retain the operation's other preconditions.

- `replay_limit`: a write above the declared replay-processing limit ([P/01.3-R035 «Waits of the doors»](#n2-doors): the limit and its unit are declared by the implementation), before admission; `Retry-After` is the time until admission in seconds, computed by the implementation. Caller action: repeat not before that deadline.

**Flag purposes.** [forms/daemon-flags.tsv](../forms/daemon-flags.tsv) alone owns the closed set, types, defaults, requiredness, commands and refusal predicates. `-dir` names the data directory (R181); `-id` is the member name in `members`, `voters`, `leader_id`. The socket commands of `admin_ops` find `admin.sock` by `-sockets`; local `recover` does not. `-rights` names the rights file; `-tls` the certificate-kit root (N1.6). `-raft` names the advertised Raft address, `-raft-bind` its listener; `-api` and `-api-bind` follow R409. `-bootstrap` starts the first member, `-join` names a member's API address, `-group-size` declares the size (R053–R061). `-door` and `-voters` follow R074; `-tuning` R052; `-leader-wait` R063. `-max-value` is the row ceiling (R146, R373), `-max-body` the entity-body limit (R319); `-max-conns`, `-api-conns`, `-api-per-address` are the connection limits (R008). `-force` follows R352/R368; `-isolated` R262; `-upper` R263. `-peers` names the recovered membership: remaining ids with Raft/API addresses, including `-id`. `--from` is the immutable copy input; `-index-base` follows R143/R300. `-groups` belongs to `rights`.

- `daemon.refuse_start` — If a voter is started with a door certificate, then the daemon MUST refuse to start.
- `daemon.refuse_start` — If `-door` is given without `-voters`, then the daemon MUST refuse to start.
- `daemon.refuse_start` — If there is no `-dir`, then the daemon MUST refuse to start.
- `daemon.refuse_start` — If there is no `-id` and no `SERVER_NAME`, then the daemon MUST refuse to start.
- `daemon.refuse_start` — If there is no `-id` with `-join`, `-door` or `-group-size 3` | `5`, then the daemon MUST refuse to start.

- `daemon.refuse_start` — If the directory holds the phase mark of an interrupted `recover` (N3 «recover the store» step 1), then the daemon MUST refuse to start.

- `daemon.refuse_start` — If flags of a start mode that the build or the mode does not have are given (R164–R167), then the daemon MUST refuse to start.

- `group.identity` — An additional transport secret is decided by the implementation («Implementation decides» item 1).

- `sockets` — An inherited `<role>.sock` has the group of the role: `SocketGroup=` of its unit (P/01.2-R109); the daemon does not change its mode or group.

- `door` — A door without a vote holds no replica of the rows.
- `door` — The door MUST write this row itself: by a request to the leader over mTLS with its own role `configstore-door` (forwarding of roles of chapter 1.2 N3).
- `door` — The write of this row MUST be the command `put` of its own row without `cas` and `guard`, the only element `seen_at`.
- `door` — If the role `configstore-door` makes any other write, a batch `op: batch` included, then it MUST get 403.
- `door` — `Cmd.id` of the replay memory (P/01.1) is not an identity: the daemon MUST NOT compare it with the server.
- `door` — The door MUST NOT forward the requests of `admin.sock`.
- `door` — If a door row does not read in its own form, then it MUST NOT be counted as a visible door.

- `format` — When the daemon starts and the directory is empty, it MUST write `FORMAT`.
- `format` — When the daemon starts, `format` and `version` are those that this build reads and the start mode is that of the directory (R402), it MUST start.

- `format` — If the directory is not empty but there is no `FORMAT`, then the daemon MUST refuse to start, code 2; the log names the directory and the mark found; nothing is written to or removed from the directory.

- `format` — If `format` or `version` of `FORMAT` is foreign, then the daemon MUST refuse to start, code 2; the log names the directory and the mark found; nothing is written to or removed from the directory.
- `format` — If `FORMAT` is out of form, then the daemon MUST refuse to start, code 2; the log names the directory and the mark found; nothing is written to or removed from the directory.

- `format` — If the daemon starts in another start mode on a non-empty directory, then it MUST refuse to start with `start_format`, code 2; the log names the directory and the mode found; nothing is written to or removed from the directory.

- `format` — If an offline `import` or `restore` goes into a directory of a group or a door, or `recover` into a directory of a box or a door, then it MUST be a refusal with `start_format`, code ≠ 0; nothing changes.
- `format` — A change of the start mode of a directory MUST go only by a copy (`copy`) into a fresh directory, as a change of implementation (R092).
- `copy` — The first line of the copy MUST be the header `{"format": "w2c-configstore-copy", "version": 1, "index": <version>}`.
- `copy` — `index` of the header is the version of the store at which the copy is taken, a JSON string as `Version` of chapter 1.1.
- `copy` — `index` of the header MUST NOT be smaller than the `index` of any row of the copy.

- `copy` — The writer MUST put the keys in ascending order of UTF-8 bytes.
- `copy` — `platform/epoch_floor` is included as an ordinary input row for upper and the `generation_at` clock check.
- `copy` — `platform/epoch_floor` of the input MUST NOT be transferred.
- `copy` — The id replay memory (chapter 1.1 N3) MUST NOT be part of the copy.
- `copy` — The copy knows no manifests: rows of any families; a family check at import is not needed (R148).
- `copy` — If the input has an extra or a missing field, then the whole input MUST be refused before the first write (N4).
- `copy` — If an input line is not JSON, not by `Row`, uses CRLF or reaches EOF before its LF (P/01.3-R093), then the whole input MUST be refused as `copy_input` before the first write.
- `copy` — If the input has a repeated key, then the whole input MUST be refused before the first write (N4).
- `copy` — If the input has an `index` of a row higher than the `index` of the header, then the whole input MUST be refused before the first write (N4).
- `copy` — If an unreadable row is in the input, then the input MUST also be refused (N4).
- `copy` — A copy of one implementation MUST be restorable by another.
- `batch` — The copy `copy` MUST be taken between batches: it carries no half of a batch.
- `admission` — The admission time MUST be in the raft snapshot together with the rows: the snapshot carries the admission time of the last record that entered it.
- `admission` — A daemon raised from the raft snapshot MUST continue from the admission time that the snapshot carries.
- `admission` — The copy `copy` MUST NOT carry the admission time (chapter 1.1 N3).
- `admission` — While the flag stands, writes with `not_after` by the writers' clocks get `expired`: the leader's clock went ahead and came back.
- `admin_ops` — `backup <file>` MUST write the file by R229 (0600) and R388 (tmp + rename).
- `admin_ops` — `status`, `backup` and `leave` of oneself MAY run at any member.
- `admin_ops` — If the CLI sends such a request at a follower, then the CLI MUST be a refusal, code ≠ 0; nothing changes.
- `admin_ops` — The visible `admin_not_leader` refusal MUST follow request/identity/body-form errors but precede write-checks.tsv, membership errors and reading an import/restore copy.
- `admin_ops` — For join/leave the body id MUST distinguish oneself (R119) from another member before `admin_not_leader` can apply.

- `floor.generation` — An epoch row of upper and of the checks of `import`, `restore` and `recover` MUST be the epoch row of never of chapter 1.2 (P/01.2-R068, P/01.2-R122, P/01.2-R123): `<x>/epoch/<y>`, an empty `<y>` included, not only the rows `<sub>/epoch/<id>` of P/03.2 N1.5.

- `floor.generation` — upper MUST be the maximum of `floor` of the row `platform/epoch_floor` and `epoch` of every epoch row (R408) in the whole verified input and in the saved state of the daemon (a fresh group has none); not a single row — 0; upper ≥ the current floor and all saved epochs.
- `floor.generation` — If there is no reliable bound of the lost tail, then the recovery MUST be refused.
- `floor.when` — The row `platform/epoch_floor` MUST NOT be written by `put`/`delete`.
- `floor.when` — The floor MUST only grow.
- `floor.when` — `-force` allows only the clock going back: with `-force` a clock earlier than `generation_at` does not refuse the raise; a uint64 overflow stays a refusal (R027, R270).
- `floor.when` — `-force` MUST NOT allow a repeat or a lowering of the generation.
- `floor.when` — `-force` MUST NOT allow a parallel recovery.
- `floor.when` — If the current row `platform/epoch_floor` does not read so, then `restore`, `import` and `recover` MUST report it as `recovery_unsafe`; the current floor is not reset.
- `floor.form` — Epochs are JSON integers < 2^53, so the floor leaves 2^32 numbers above itself: the generation MUST be ≤ 2^21 − 1 (hours since 2026-01-01 suffice for ~239 years).
- `floor.form` — If a generation would give more, then the recovery MUST be refused, as an overflow.

- `floor.issue` — An issue that read the floor before the raise can write a number below the floor — the worker does not start such an epoch: a confirmation after the write (P/03.2 N3 «take_epoch(id)»).
- `import` (door_rows) — A door row in the input MUST be transferred like a row of any family; the live door rewrites its own.

- `import` (base) — The base of new versions of `restore` is `index` of the header of the copy (`restore` has no `-index-base`): every write after the transfer MUST get a version above it and above any version of the group.
- `import` (base) — `-index-base` MUST be ≥ the greatest version of the input.
- `import` (base) — `-index-base` is the start of new versions: every write after the transfer MUST get a version above the base and above any version of the group.

- `import` (base) — Copy versions may coincide with versions previously issued for fresh-group door rows. A door row MAY return to a lower version; the door rewrites it without cas above the base within 30 s (R290).
- `import` (check) — If a key of an input row is not by chapter 1.1 N1, then `import` and `restore` MUST refuse without changes.
- `import` (check) — If the size of an input row is above the row ceiling (R146, R373), then `import` and `restore` MUST refuse without changes.

- `import` (check) — On a box the row ceiling of the check MUST be `-max-value` of the command `import`/`restore`, its default is that of the daemon in [forms/daemon-flags.tsv](../forms/daemon-flags.tsv).
- `import` (check) — In a group the row ceiling of the check MUST be the effective `-max-value` of the leader.
- `import` (check) — If an epoch row (R408) has `epoch` not a decimal integer, then upper is not reliable and the whole input MUST be refused.
- `import` (check) — If `platform/epoch_floor` has `floor` not decimal, then upper is not reliable and the whole input MUST be refused.
- `import` (check) — If an epoch or floor row is unreadable (outcomes of the families `epoch`, `epoch_floor`), then upper is not reliable and the whole input MUST be refused.
- `import` (families) — The copy knows no manifests: `import` MUST NOT check the families of rows; a row of any family is transferred.

- `import` (floor_first) — For import/restore in either mode, the first write MUST be new F1: index above the base and all destination-issued versions, generation_at at the raise. Continuation keeps its exact index (R151); other input rows keep copy versions (R140).
- `import` (replay) — A partial replay MUST NOT copy back the old floor.
- `import` (replay) — A partial replay MUST NOT raise F1 again.
- `import` (replay) — A failure after F1 may leave partial rows. The same input bytes MUST continue that attempt with the same floor; byte-comparison mechanism is the implementation's choice.
- `import` (replay) — If another input comes before «Done», then it MUST be a refusal without changes (`import_other_input`, code ≠ 0).
- `import` (held_writers.group) — A group MUST hold writers until continuation through the leader's admin.sock: 503 `unavailable` (`import_held`), as R413 requires.
- `import` (held_writers.group) — The wait of held writers MUST obey the declared budget.
- `import` (held_writers.group) — While writers are held, reads MUST answer as the store `file://` (R159).
- `import` (held_writers.group) — If the majority is lost while writers are held, then the way out is `recover` (N3 «recover the store»).
- `import` (held_writers.group) — In a group `restore` MUST follow the same rule, because its phases are common with `import`.
- `metrics` — An alarm of the voters is: membership ≠ declared.
- `metrics` — An alarm of the voters is: more than `RAFT_ELECTION_ALARM_COUNT` elections in `RAFT_ELECTION_ALARM_WINDOW`.

- `metrics` — The alarms of the voters (R161, R304, R305) are rules of a reader of `/metrics` of all voters of the group over the series of [forms/metrics.tsv](../forms/metrics.tsv); the daemon does not raise them: it gives no series or log entry for them beyond that table.

- `metrics` — The lag of a follower F (R304) MUST be `configstore_raft_index{kind="commit"}` of the leader minus `configstore_raft_index{kind="applied"}` of F, both of one reading; a follower cut off from the records lags even when its own commit equals its applied.
- `box` — `/metrics` of a box MUST give the series of [forms/metrics.tsv](../forms/metrics.tsv) with the values of one member (the values of the emitter `box`).
- `box` — `join` of its own id MUST give 200 `{}`.
- `box` — `join` of a foreign id MUST give 409 `refused`, even with `-force`.
- `box` — `leave` MUST give 409 `refused` («the last voter»).
- `box` — `admit` MUST be a refusal, code ≠ 0.
- `box` — `recover` MUST be a refusal, code 2 («this build has no raft»): a box has no group, there is nothing to recover it with, a copy — `import`.
- `box` — `import`/`restore` on a box MUST write the floor as the first write, then the rows.
- `repeat` — If `join` comes for an id with another Raft address, then it MUST be 409 `refused`, without changes.
- `repeat` — If `leave` comes for an unknown id, then it MUST be 409 `refused`, without changes.
- Acquisition MUST be atomic: among simultaneous starts on one directory, including an empty one, exactly one becomes owner.
- Ownership MUST be checked first among refusal reasons that depend on the directory.

- If a second daemon starts on a live-owned directory, then it MUST refuse with `start_data_dir_owned`, separately from `start_format`: before readiness and before any write, including `FORMAT`; it names the directory in the log.
- If a second daemon starts on a live-owned directory, then it MUST leave the first daemon and its data untouched and MUST NOT take over its ownership.
- Other existing refusal reasons, including `start_format` and, on a box, unfinished `import`/`restore`, remain.
- The positive restart is tested on a healthy completed state; unfinished transfer on a box is a separate negative case.
The effective `-leader-wait` and connection-limit defaults MUST be owned by [daemon-flags.tsv](../forms/daemon-flags.tsv).
- `Status.state` keeps its separate Leader/Follower/Candidate/Shutdown/Door spelling.
- The values of the series are the column `value_rule` of [forms/metrics.tsv](../forms/metrics.tsv).
- An implementation MAY emit only the current-state sample of `configstore_raft_state` or also zero-valued other states.
- `# TYPE` metadata is optional; when present, it MUST be the column `type` of [forms/metrics.tsv](../forms/metrics.tsv).
- The existing series names, label escaping and required observations remain unchanged.

- When `-api-bind` is given, the daemon MUST listen for the service doors of N2 on `-api-bind` and keep `-api` as the address it names to its partners: the value of `members` and `leader` in `/v1/status`, the address of its join, the same as `-raft` and `-raft-bind`.

- The name of a start refusal by the form MUST be: a flag outside the table or of another command, a repeated flag, a `bool` with a value, a positional word, a value out of its type and an unmet `required` — `start_flags`; a true `bad` — `start_config`.

- The exceptions are named by N4: `-group-size` out of its form and `-tls` required by an address off the loopback or by `-join` — `start_config`; at `recover` — `recover_isolated`, `recover_upper`, `recover_peers`.
- If there are several violations, then the refusal MUST be by the first flag in the order of the rows of the form, within a row: type → `required` → `bad`.
- A deployment MAY set other positive limits before the run starts and names them in the description.
- If the connection limit is exceeded, then the daemon MUST answer 503 `unavailable` with `Retry-After: 1` (chapter 1.1 N4).
- `admin.sock` MUST have its own limit declared by the implementation (item 8 of «Implementation decides»).
- If the limit of `admin.sock` is exceeded, then it MUST be the common `connection_limit`: 503 `unavailable` with `Retry-After`.
- The name of a flag is exactly as the table writes it (`--from` with two hyphens).
- A flag of the type `bool` is written without a value (`-door=true` is a refusal).
- `--` alone ends the flags.
- If a flag is repeated, then the daemon MUST refuse to start, code 2.
- If a flag is a flag of another command, then the daemon MUST refuse to start, code 2.
- If a flag has a value out of its type, then the daemon MUST refuse to start, code 2.
- If the daemon gets a positional word, then it MUST refuse to start, code 2; positional words are only those of `admin_ops` by its grammar above (`admit <id>`, `backup <file>`, `leave [id]`).

- The values `bytes` and `int` MUST be a decimal integer without a sign, a plus or leading zeros (`0` itself is allowed), `bytes` without a unit suffix (`512KiB` is the writing of the prose, not a value).
- The value `duration` MUST be `<integer><unit>`, the unit `ms`, `s`, `m` or `h`, greater than `0` (`5s`, `250ms`).
- The value `addr` MUST be `host:port`, a non-empty host (a name, IPv4 or `[IPv6]`) and a decimal port `1`–`65535`.
- The default of `-id` and the absence of a default MUST be defined only by its row and header in [daemon-flags.tsv](../forms/daemon-flags.tsv).

The form of a certificate, the closed list of signatures, the kit, revocation and the next CA are the common [role certificate contract](../../common/contracts/role-certificate.md)\n(`cert`, `sig`, `kit`, `revoke`, `rotation`). The daemon verifies the peer by it; the roles of the daemon:

```yaml
roles:        configstore, configstore-door
raft:         configstore
api:          configstore, configstore-door
counts:       the daemon log
```

- `roles` — The roles of the daemon are `configstore` and `configstore-door`; they MUST come with `-tls` for group traffic and every non-loopback declared or listening address (`-api`, `-raft`, `-api-bind`, `-raft-bind`); local loopback box doors MAY run without `-tls`.
The doors of the chapter are at the store daemon (chapter 1.1: `/v1/get`, `/v1/list`, `/v1/write`) and its service doors:
HTTP contract: [01-store.api.openapi.yaml](01-store.api.openapi.yaml).
All own JSON answers have full schemas, metrics are text/plain, without a fictitious empty JSON instead of text.

- `POST /v1/write` — A floor request refused before application MUST NOT occupy its `id`; only an applied raise enters the replay memory of P/01.3-R216. Admission metadata follows P/01.1-R070 independently of replay memory.
- `POST /v1/write` — A durable replay memory of `op: floor` MUST survive a daemon restart.
- `POST /v1/write` — If a new `id` comes with `floor` ≤ the current one, then it MUST be 409 `refused` (a row of chapter 1.1 N4).
- Unknown fields of the body of a service POST are rejected: if a body has unknown fields, then the door MUST answer 400.
- If the body of a service POST has extra JSON, then the door MUST answer 400.
- For own status/join/leave/write/metrics a 503 before sending MUST be `UnavailableFault`.
- `backup` MUST publish the temporary file by rename, only after success.
- If `backup` fails or is cancelled, then the former published copy MUST stay: a refusal does not replace it.
- The temporary file of `backup` MUST be removed on failure and on cancellation.
- A leftover temporary file of `backup` MUST be removed by the next run of `backup` to the same target, because the daemon does not know that file.
- The result of `restore`/`import` MUST be code 0 only after a full check of the transfer, otherwise non-zero with the phase and the path.

- A correct GET on an ordinary role socket MUST return exactly `403 ForbiddenFault` (the row `sc-copy_admin_only` of [forms/service-checks.tsv](../forms/service-checks.tsv)) before opening or exposing a snapshot.
- The body of the success MUST be the existing UTF-8/LF `w2c-configstore-copy`, version 1, without a private prelude.
- The copy of the success MUST be at one consistent index.
- An exact `Content-Length` or valid completed chunked transfer MUST be used; connection close alone is not successful framing.
- The answer to HEAD on this path has no body.
- If a failure happens after `200` headers of chunked output, then the daemon MUST NOT send a final zero chunk.
- If a failure happens after `200` headers of a Content-Length response, then the daemon MUST NOT give a false complete Content-Length response.
- Completion MUST NOT be signalled before the whole artifact.
- The backup CLI MUST validate the whole existing copy grammar.
- The backup CLI MUST write the temporary file and publish it by R229 (`0600`), R388 (rename only after success) and R389 (failure/cancellation preserves the previous published file).
- There is no new HTTP import/restore or compatible private copy alias.
- Other internal named/versioned read-fence/admit/import frames remain allowed by «Implementation decides» item 1; this HTTP operation is the narrow exception for the copy transfer itself.
- The implementation MUST declare a finite response-write budget.

- A reader that does not take the response within the response-write budget MUST lose the connection; the client side is `no_reply` of the [store client contract](../../common/contracts/store-client.md).
- The implementation MUST declare a finite wait for the commit of a write under a live leader.
- The total time of the attempts of one request of a door without a vote MUST NOT be less than the effective `-leader-wait` interval.
- The implementation MUST declare the number of attempts of a door without a vote.
- A write without an `id` that the door does not retry MUST stay `ambiguous`.
- The attempts are an internal step of the door, not a level of the client retries of the store client contract.
- All attempts of a door MUST fit within the end-to-end deadline of the caller.
- The loss of the answer to an attempt already sent MUST stay `ambiguous`.
- The doors of this chapter MUST obey the end-to-end budget of the [store client contract](../../common/contracts/store-client.md#production-obligations).
- The implementation MUST declare a finite limit on the processing of replays and its unit.
- On a full disk a write MUST get 503 `unavailable` (`disk_full` of N4) only on a proven refusal before the effect, without a partial result (chapter 1.1 N4).
- On a full disk, after the effect or with an unknown result, the `ambiguous_*` outcomes and the repeat of the barriers MUST apply (chapter 1.1 R144).
- A read MUST keep working while there is a leader and a quorum.
- A read mechanism that needs a write is declared by the implementation.
- After space is freed writes MUST return without a restart.
- When descriptors are exhausted, requests already started MUST get their own definite outcome, and the daemon does not crash.
- Step 0: the operator saves the original directories/copy.
- Step 0: the operator checks upper and the whole input.
- Step 0: the confirmation of isolation is the flag `-isolated` of the command `recover`: if it is absent, then `recover` MUST refuse before changes, code ≠ 0.
- Step 0: a bound of the lost tail known to the operator is `-upper N`; it MUST only raise the computed upper; if it is below the computed one, then a refusal before changes.
- Step 0: mutual exclusion of runs of recover/restore/import is item 6 of «Implementation decides».
- Step 1: `recover` MUST remove the membership of the absent members in the Raft configuration.
- Step 1: `recover` MUST remove the addresses of the absent members in `members`.
- Step 1: `recover` MUST remove the leave/admit marks of the absent members.
- Step 1: `recover` MUST keep the rows of the row store of any family, `platform/configstore-doors/<id>` included.
- Step 1: `recover` MUST raise `platform/epoch_floor` by a generation.
- Step 1: a partial dump gives no upper bound.
- Step 1: while the mark stands, a repeat of `recover` MUST start over.
- Step 1: after such a `recover`, a repeat of the former attempt with its floor F1 MUST refuse.
- Step 1: writers MUST stay held until the new `import` attempt completes.
- Step 2: the others join one by one from new empty directories after the old ones are saved (the second/fourth — with `-force` at a transitional evenness, not beyond the declared size).
- Step 3: those who return after `leave` — `admit`.
- `-force` cancels none of these checks.
- If a reliable upper of the lost tail cannot be obtained, then the guarantee of non-repetition of epochs is unprovable and recovery by this profile MUST NOT be performed.
- Blocking external output MUST run outside the lock that serializes ordinary mutations.
- The implementation declares finite bounds for lock wait, output, cancellation and orderly stop.
- A stalled receiver MUST NOT retain the mutation lock until transmission finishes.
- Success, failure and cancellation MUST release snapshot and transport ownership.
- An unrelated operation may keep its existing bounded pre-effect refusal; that response alone does not prove correct lock scope.
- On stop, connections whose request has not been read MUST be closed.
- On stop, the daemon MUST cancel or bound external I/O.
- On stop, the daemon MUST resolve or classify admitted work by its existing definite/ambiguous outcomes.
- On stop, the daemon MUST retire owned snapshots, connections and listeners within the declared orderly-stop bound.
- The orderly-stop bound MUST fit below the actual service-manager stop deadline with a separately measured teardown margin.

`store-copy-floor` uses the actual durable backup/import/continuation paths. First restore a valid seed, take a real backup of that restored store with its existing floor and at least two other rows, then import that immutable backup into a fresh destination. Interrupt I/O after one non-floor target row has been durably transferred; close and continue the same attempt with the same input. Capture the first new floor row F1, including items/index/generation_at, and compare it after continuation. Inspect actual write order, every non-floor row/version, completeness and absence of an old-floor transfer. Use a controlled wall clock; no canned backup/import result or fabricated expected observation. A panic, unrelated failure or unexecuted path fails.

`store-copy-floor` использует настоящие прочные backup/import/продолжение. Восстановить валидный исходный вход, снять настоящую backup-копию уже восстановленного хранилища с его floor и хотя бы двумя прочими строками, импортировать неизменную копию в свежий каталог. Прервать I/O после прочного переноса одной строки кроме пола; закрыть и продолжить ту же попытку с тем же входом. Снять первую новую строку F1, включая items/index/generation_at, сравнить её после продолжения. Наблюдать реальный порядок записей, все прочие строки/версии, полноту и отсутствие переноса старого пола. Часы управляемые; готовые результаты backup/import и вымышленные наблюдения не допускаются. Паника, посторонняя ошибка и неисполненный путь проваливают шов.

**Membership outcomes.** Valid requests obey R016/R413 and the availability/unknown-result rules R063/R228/R234. Box: own join 200, foreign join 409 even with force, leave 409, admit non-zero (P/01.3-R169). Door: join/leave 409, admit non-zero (R087/R417). Follower admin: own join/leave by R119; another id's join/leave and any admit refuse by R118/R235. A peer may leave only itself; another id requires leader admin.sock (R214). At the leader, join of a left id is 403 until admit; current id/same Raft address — 200 with API update, another Raft address — 409; a new id — 200 subject to P/01.3-R054. Leave: known non-last voter — 200, unknown or last — 409. Admit of an already admitted correct id is no-op exit 0 (R177); a left id gets permission to rejoin after confirmation, exit 0 (R234), without joining it or changing rows.

removed: For the bindings of the target `P/01/production` the words of the payload mean the following. The boundary `admission_time` is the wall clock of the daemon process that P/01.1 N3 «Admission time» reads at admission: the provider observes this clock domain of the process, and the admission time that the daemon stores is judged by the public outcomes of the case, not by the provider. The resource `heap` is the resident anonymous memory of the process (`RssAnon` of `/proc/<pid>/status`), and `memory` is its resident set (`VmRSS`); a heap figure of a language runtime is no resource of the form. With the latch `sink` the provider is the reader of the output, and `cancel` is its deactivation: the provider closes the sink at `deactivate`, the `monotonic_ns` of the deactivation record is that moment, and no observation carries `cancel`. The phase `recover_mark` names no file: the mark is the first changing step of `recover` in `-dir` (P/01.3 R021), and the point of the fault is the first change of `-dir` after the first top-level entry that `recover` completes, so neither the payload nor the invocation carries a name of the mark. The phase `copy_after_headers` is the end of the stream as the client receives it after the complete header block of a `200`, made between the daemon and the client: it gives the half of `RUN-H03` that the CLI judges. The half of the daemon after `200`, only an incomplete close and no second fault, is judged on its own stream under the cancellation, the stalled sink and the stop that the judge makes; a failure inside the daemon has no binding.

removed: Для привязок цели `P/01/production` слова payload значат следующее. Граница `admission_time` — стенные часы процесса демона, которые P/01.1 N3 «Admission time» читает при допуске: provider наблюдает этот домен часов процесса, а время допуска, которое хранит демон, судится публичными исходами случая, не provider. Ресурс `heap` — резидентная анонимная память процесса (`RssAnon` из `/proc/<pid>/status`), а `memory` — его резидентный набор (`VmRSS`); показатель кучи среды исполнения языка ресурсом формы не является. При latch `sink` provider — читатель вывода, а `cancel` — его деактивация: provider закрывает sink на `deactivate`, `monotonic_ns` записи деактивации — этот момент, и ни одно наблюдение `cancel` не несёт. Фаза `recover_mark` не называет файла: метка — первый изменяющий шаг `recover` в `-dir` (P/01.3 R021), а точка сбоя — первое изменение `-dir` после первой записи верхнего уровня, которую `recover` завершил; поэтому ни payload, ни вызов имени метки не несут. Фаза `copy_after_headers` — конец потока, как его получает клиент после полного блока заголовков ответа `200`, сделанный между демоном и клиентом: она даёт ту половину `RUN-H03`, которую судит CLI. Половина демона после `200` — только неполное закрытие и никакого второго отказа — судится на его собственном потоке при отмене, застое sink и остановке, которые делает судья; у сбоя внутри демона привязки нет.
